objective: A local k6 load test of the site's main read and write paths that reports P95 and P99 latency per endpoint and fails when either regresses past a set percentage against the previous run on the same machine, started by one PowerShell line, generating no AWS or Cognito traffic: virtual users authenticate with ID tokens signed by a local test key, which the backend accepts only when ENVIRONMENT is exactly "perf".
acceptance_criteria: Settings gains environment (env ENVIRONMENT, default empty) and perf_jwks_path (env PERF_JWKS_PATH, default empty). Settings construction fails when perf_jwks_path is set and environment is not exactly "perf" (including empty, "development", "production" and "Perf").

When perf_jwks_path is set (so environment is "perf"), get_token_verifier returns a CognitoTokenVerifier built from the JWKS JSON file at that path, with the perf issuer and audience; it never fetches a JWKS over the network. When perf_jwks_path is empty, get_token_verifier is unchanged: the RefreshingTokenVerifier from the Cognito settings.

The perf verifier keeps every check CognitoTokenVerifier already makes (RS256 only, the five required claims, token_use "id", aud present): a token signed by a key not in the perf JWKS, an expired token, an HS256 token and an access token are each refused with 401 on GET /users/me.

backend/scripts/mint_perf_tokens.py, refusing to run unless ENVIRONMENT is exactly "perf", generates a fresh RSA key pair, writes the public JWKS and one ID token per perf user (cognito sub perf-user-<n>, n from 1 to --count, exp at least 2 hours) as JSON files into --out-dir. It writes the private key nowhere else and never prints a token.

backend/scripts/seed_perf.py refuses to run unless ENVIRONMENT is "development" or "perf" and is idempotent (a second run adds no rows). It seeds synthetic teams and games under an id range documented in the script that no nba.com id uses, at least 300 users whose cognito subs match the minted tokens and whose created_at is more than SPAM_NEW_ACCOUNT_HOURS old, follows between them, at least 20,000 posts including replies and reposts, likes, and posts mentioning games (#GameId<id>), in bulk statements rather than one ORM insert per row.

perf/ holds the k6 scripts. The scenarios, weighted like real use, are feed read, game page, search, profile and post creation; post creation uses text unique per iteration with no link. Every request is tagged with its endpoint. Profiles: smoke (1 VU, 1 minute), load (steady), stress (ramping, aborted once http_req_failed crosses its limit). Thresholds are set per endpoint tag on http_req_duration p(95) and p(99), plus http_req_failed. The summary is written as JSON under perf/results/.

backend/scripts/perf_compare.py (stdlib only) compares a run's summary with a baseline summary and exits non-zero when any endpoint's p95 or p99 regressed by more than --max-regression percent (default 20), printing a per-endpoint table; with no baseline present it stores the run as the baseline and exits 0. An endpoint present in the baseline but missing from the run is a failure.

perf/run.ps1 is the one-line entry point (powershell -File perf/run.ps1 -Profile smoke|load|stress), working in Windows PowerShell 5.1 and pwsh 7 on Linux: mint tokens, bring up the compose perf profile, wait for backend-perf's /health, seed, run k6, compare, and always run docker compose --profile perf down, even on failure. It targets backend-perf only; no URL in perf/ points at fanwire.daviddems.com or any AWS endpoint.
An infra test on the synthesized stacks proves no deployed Lambda function sets ENVIRONMENT to "perf" or sets PERF_JWKS_PATH at all.
